about: Every experiment from the design discussion, each tied to the decision it settles. Costs are rough and assume today's den: four Hue lights, no engineered fixture installed, physical output of engineered fixtures needs a separate owner approval.

experiments.name: Log every correction with its context
experiments.how: Capture every human action on the real lights as one Correction, with its changes, the last decision, person states, light state and whose light it was; den_lighting's per-bulb holds are the raw events. After a few weeks hand-sort a sample into the five links or cannot tell, with whose light it was, and compare with the automatic attribution; report abstention and shared rates, and whether glare (comfort) corrections can be told from preference, a class that needs the changer's report as its reference.
experiments.decides: Whether attribution is reliable enough for corrections to train perception and need, or only preferences, and how many corrections can be learned from at all; whether they may then train perception and need is the owner's decision {{dec:learning-permissions}}.
experiments.cost: cheap; extends the virtual den's decision-bound correction log to real lights

experiments.name: Crossing study
experiments.how: Stage 20–30 crossings and occlusions. Count identity switches with geometry only; the body-appearance and face arms run only after the owner's decision {{dec:learning-permissions}}; record how often a face is even visible.
experiments.decides: Whether face would earn a place in tracking or only in naming tracks, if the owner allows either {{dec:learning-permissions}}.
experiments.cost: an evening of staged walks plus labeling

experiments.name: Need from geometry alone
experiments.how: A simple model of 'focused task at a surface' from pose, hands, objects and dwell, compared with Qwen on a small owner-confirmed set, scoring demand per band (fine recall, coverage) as well as calibration.
experiments.decides: How much a large vision-language model is needed for the states lighting cares about.

experiments.name: Student backbone ablation
experiments.how: Need heads on pose, objects and geometry alone; then adding V-JEPA features; then a small vision-language model's image features. Score on the confirmed set and on predicting corrections.
experiments.decides: Which on-device model, and whether V-JEPA earns its GPU.
experiments.cost: weeks; needs logged bundles and the gold set

experiments.name: Edge budget run
experiments.how: Run the candidate perception stack on the Orin Nano in Victoria or a 16 GB Orin NX; measure rate, latency and power per stage.
experiments.decides: The hardware class. Deliberately later: build the great system first.

experiments.name: A real Qwen latency benchmark
experiments.how: Vary clip length (4–30 frames), answer length (short JSON vs free text), cold vs warm, with no cache reuse. For per-person requests, a paced replay of recorded sessions at the declared single-track cadence (one request per 4 s) measures each request's service time; only the capture-to-request schedule is emulated. The whole-room stills receipt (1.25 s median, 1.97 s p95) times a different workload, so it does not qualify the per-person requests [[R3]].
experiments.decides: Qwen's live role and how many teaching calls are affordable.
experiments.cost: a day on the LA GPU, scheduled around voice

experiments.name: Channel contribution capture
experiments.how: Lock exposure and white balance, read linear values, subtract an all-off frame, step each channel through its dimming levels; check whether channels of one type share one dimming curve, and whether the sum predicts a mixed scene, including scenes near full combined output. Frames are normalised under the same version as the camera scale (`normalisation_version` `meter-norm/v1`).
experiments.decides: Whether the camera can be the room's light sensor, and whether locked exposure plus differencing beats the three failed footprint runs.
experiments.cost: cheap; can start on the den's four Hue lights with den_lighting paused while the room is empty, its saved normal scene written back from a pre-probe snapshot before resume

experiments.name: Camera-meter calibration and a day of daylight
experiments.how: Fix the camera scale `k_L` from one grey card of known reflectance and one lux-meter reading at the card, pass the known-card round trip, and hold back later days and the other meter points (desk and sofa) as checks against a tolerance in lux fixed beforehand {{dec:photometry-commissioning}}; then track window daylight for a full day against sun position and blind state.
experiments.decides: Whether camera estimates can be absolute (the round trip and the held-out checks in lux are both needed; a passing relative camera score establishes neither), and how daylight is modelled.

experiments.name: Aim verification
experiments.how: Predicted versus observed spot position for the gimbal spot, including shadowing by the person, predicted with the person's nominal body envelope (versioned); first, the fixture's stop, aim-readback and fade-pre-emption capabilities, which stay unknown until measured {{dec:fixture-capabilities}}.
experiments.decides: Whether verify can catch delivery errors on the spot.
experiments.cost: cheap once a gimbal fixture is installed (none in the den today)

experiments.name: Coordinator v0 against today's Hue policy, on replay
experiments.how: Guidance targets plus the light model and an optimizer, scored by replay against the scenes the frozen den_lighting version showed on the same logged evenings, with each evening's actual holds pinned in both arms and both arms run through the same Hue light model: anticipation and stability as replay surrogates against floors fixed before the run, and predicted service coverage and missed service at the owner's marks on gold-labelled replay sessions, labelled 'predicted, replay surrogate'. Corrections per occupied hour come only from rung 11's canary. A virtual-den run against the rule table (assumed photometry) is a separate, separately versioned synthetic claim (`comparator.kind = synthetic`).
experiments.decides: Whether optimizing is promising enough to earn the real-light canary.
experiments.cost: weeks of logged evenings; a virtual-den run is a separate synthetic check

experiments.name: The DP session
experiments.how: A lighting designer or DP lights the den with its fixtures for four or five moments, narrating why; capture fixed-exposure images, settings and reasons; check whether a weighted objective lands near their choices.
experiments.decides: How far simple weights on perceptual terms go.

experiments.name: Taste agreement
experiments.how: Show designers and ordinary people the same pairs of scenes.
experiments.decides: If designers agree with each other far more than users do, taste should come from experts and comfort from users.

experiments.name: Automatic commissioning
experiments.how: From the den scan, detect surfaces and focal points, generate three looks, compare side by side with the DP's.
experiments.decides: Whether day-one beauty can be generated automatically.

experiments.name: Intent transfer
experiments.how: Apply the same looks to a second room (the LA living room) without re-tuning.
experiments.decides: Whether looks in perceptual terms really transfer between rooms.

experiments.name: Radial zone probe
experiments.how: Light each radial zone alone at locked exposure, fit anchor angle and order, compare with the owner's call.
experiments.decides: Whether zone orientation can be measured instead of judged.
experiments.cost: minutes once an engineered fixture is installed; physical output needs owner approval

experiments.name: Spotlight as wand
experiments.how: Sweep pan and tilt; fit the commanded angles to the 3D landing points (at least four well-spread aims) for fixture position and gimbal zeros; compare with tape.
experiments.decides: Whether the tape-measure worksheet can go.
experiments.cost: cheap once a gimbal fixture is installed

experiments.name: Blink identification
experiments.how: Blink each channel in a unique pattern and match smart-home entities to physical channels automatically. The run aborts on the occupancy gate or on any state change it did not send, and no remaining flash or restore overwrites a light a person changed.
experiments.decides: Safe automatic entity mapping (the repo refuses mapping by name).
experiments.cost: cheap; can start on the four Hue lights with den_lighting paused, its saved normal scene written back from a pre-probe snapshot before resume

experiments.name: Camera-only room map
experiments.how: Build the den's rough map from OAK depth alone (planes and boxes); measure wall and table-height error against the Scaniverse mesh.
experiments.decides: Whether the phone scan can become optional.

experiments.name: Map from use
experiments.how: Infer seats, tables and floor from a few days of tracks; compare with labelled anchors.
experiments.decides: Whether use can label the room.

build_order.name: Track each person; per-person state with Qwen still interpreting
build_order.detail: Per-person tracking and PersonState, with Qwen still interpreting, now per person and within today's request caps; video and a faster rate follow E6. In the ladder it is proposed to come after an offline need test on one person (N1, N2) {{dec:need-test-order}}. Alone, this gives each person a state of their own; per-person light (a task light for A at the counter while B keeps the reading beam, instead of ambient for both) comes once coordinator v0 reads it.

build_order.name: Log at every interface
build_order.detail: Bundles, features, Qwen descriptions, person states, light states, decisions and corrections. Cheap now; it is the data every later model is trained and judged on. Keeping the camera recordings themselves, on a validated capture clock, is its own step (ladder R), which needs the owner's approval {{dec:recording-retention}} and can start first.

build_order.name: A small owner-confirmed gold set
build_order.detail: Owner-confirmed intervals per need state, refreshed now and then; model-made labels never score. A single-person part, as a fixed input and separate blind labels (ladder N1), is proposed to come first and score the early need test (N2) before any tracker {{dec:need-test-order}}; the two-person, per-track part follows tracking (rung 4), with the owner's marks of the worked patch where service is measured.

build_order.name: Measure light and build the light model
build_order.detail: E7 and E8 on the den's Hue lights, then the light model; coordinator v0 (E10) joins this with step 1's person state and is compared on replay with the den_lighting scenes shown on the Hue bulbs, through the same light model.

build_order.name: Looks from a designer
build_order.detail: The DP session (E11) seeds the first intent library; preferences learn inside its guardrails.

build_order.name: Structured-slot student
build_order.detail: Need heads on pose, objects and geometry; add V-JEPA only if the ablation (E4) says it helps.

build_order.name: Self-calibration
build_order.detail: Zone probe and spotlight wand once engineered fixtures are installed; blink identification can start earlier on the Hue lights. Manual values remain the test set.

build_order.name: Spatial memory last
build_order.detail: Per-landmark counts of episode kinds; its main job is ranking hypotheses during occlusion.
